findings.finding: Implement item 3. Doctor prints the link, its source, the host overlap and each stamp, and exits non-zero only on a host-interface overlap. That matches Decision 8's list of what doctor prints. But doctor's own contract (host.go help, cli.md) is 'exits non-zero when a required capability is unmet, so it is usable as a CI or agent gate'. On hyperv (relay boot VHDX) and vz (the prepared image), the stamped asset is required by every build, so a missing or stale stamp means every build refuses while doctor exits 0. On qemu and firecracker the stamped initramfs serves only direct boot, so a report is enough there.
findings.suggestion: Exit non-zero when a stamp is missing or stale on an asset every build of that driver needs (hyperv, vz). Keep the qemu and firecracker direct-boot stamps as reports. Or record the reason for not doing so in the design at Consolidation.

findings.finding: Implement item 8. With `--image /path/disk.img`, the stamp is looked up beside that disk, which is the right place. But the refusal's fix is PrepareCommand (`sudo warden image prepare --driver vz`), which re-prepares only the default cache's image (cmd/warden/image.go prepareVZMacos). A user with a custom image follows the fix and is refused again: a dead end on an uncommon path.
findings.suggestion: When the disk is outside the cache, name a fix that works for that path: re-prepare that image directory, or omit --image to use the prepared cache image. Or let `image prepare --driver vz` take the image directory, if a one-line ReprepareImage(dir) path is wanted. Add a table case to TestImageStamp.

findings.finding: Implement item 9. buildif_linux.go (rtnetlink dump parsing, RTM_NEWADDR/DELADDR encoding, ack handling) and dhcp_vm_linux.go (SO_BINDTODEVICE on udp/67) have no tier-0 tests. Their callers are well covered through the buildIface and packetConn fakes (vmlink_test.go, dhcp_test.go incl. FuzzDHCPReply). Opening sockets needs root and a netns, so the syscalls belong to tier 2 and native validation (the firecracker CI run and the linux-kvm and qemu-any hosts), as TEST-01 intends. The parsing and encoding are pure, though, and are where a silent bug would hide: parseRoute's RTA_DST/RTA_OIF handling, the IFA_LOCAL-over-IFA_ADDRESS choice, and the ifaddrmsg layout. A related edge: Flush deletes addresses one by one from a single dump, and on Linux deleting a primary address also deletes its secondaries in the same subnet (promote_secondaries off). The next RTM_DELADDR then fails with EADDRNOTAVAIL and the claim fails with 500. Unlikely with today's inits, which add one address.
findings.suggestion: Split the message building and parsing from the socket I/O. Test them at tier 0 with canned netlink bytes: a dump holding a default route, a /30 route on another oif and a multi-address interface, plus addrRequest's encoded bytes. In Flush, treat EADDRNOTAVAIL as already removed.

findings.finding: Implement item 6. Only Hyper-V has an end-to-end tier-0 test that its claim carries the link. qemu (driver.go:221), firecracker (driver_linux.go:218) and vz (driver.go:237) each pass `req.Link().Claim()` in one line, with no test. driver/session_link_test.go covers ClaimRelay sending what it is given. A regression that passes nil fails loudly on qemu and firecracker: the new relay-vm init leaves eth0 unaddressed, so the relay answers 400 'build_link is required'. On vz it is quiet: host mode falls back to its --subnet default 10.100.0.0/30, which the driver no longer passes, and the build still runs on a link that is not the configured one.
findings.suggestion: Add one tier-0 assertion per driver that the claim it sends carries the request's link. The order-test seams from item 5 can capture the ClaimRelay arguments, or the shared claim-building call can be factored and tested once with every driver as a caller. At minimum cover vz, the quiet case.

findings.finding: An edit merged two pseudocode lines. The firecracker relay-start step reads 'resolvers for the relay are the host's, minus loopback, host addresses and any inside the build link first take a free network slot made by `warden setup` (a host lock), ...'. The resolver sentence and main's 'first take a free network slot' line ran together.
findings.suggestion: Split it back into two steps: the resolver selection, then 'first take a free network slot made by `warden setup` (a host lock), kill VMMs a dead warden left on it, and claim the relay at the slot's upstream address'.

findings.finding: Implement item 7. A malformed `[vm] build_link` fails every command, container builds included, because it is checked as the file loads (cmd/warden/config.go:128). That behaviour is right: Decision 8 says 'a config value is checked when the file loads', and UX-08 favours failing fast on a bad config whatever the driver. It is not a redesign, since a17 is about the claim, not the key. But the reference doc says only 'The container driver ... ignores the setting', which reads as if a bad value is ignored there too.
findings.suggestion: Keep the behaviour. Reword configuration.md:101 to say the container driver ignores a valid value, and that a malformed one is refused at load by every command (as any config error is).

findings.finding: refresh-cache.sh exits 'relay boot VHDX is current' when the disk exists and relay-boot.source matches. It does not check whether relay-boot.link-channel exists. The source stamp excludes the script itself, so a disk whose link stamp is missing but whose relay source matches is never re-stamped. warden refuses it, naming refresh-cache.sh, and refresh-cache.sh says it is current: a loop. It cannot happen on this branch's own history, since the stamp line landed with relay-source changes in 19bbe69 and relay changed again later. It can happen if the stamp file is lost, or a disk is copied without it.
findings.suggestion: Require the link stamp for the 'current' short-circuit (`[ -f "$linkf" ]`, and `--check` reports it). Or have warden's fix for a missing stamp say `refresh-cache.sh --force`.

findings.finding: The change trips GLOBAL-06 (env-relay). The vm-mode relay changes its own interface from claim data, and a DHCP responder now goes live on the build link in vm mode and in host mode for vz. The design's TEST-08 list (design:1030) is the input for the security suite, but queue/security-suite.yaml does not mention build_link, the vm-mode responder or DHCP/ARP spoofing. Most of the cases have tier-0 coverage (vmlink_test.go, dhcp_test.go with FuzzDHCPReply, relaycfg/buildlink_test.go, relay/buildlink_test.go). The adversarial cases have no recorded home.
findings.suggestion: Carry the Security note's TEST-08 list into security-suite's queue item or design inputs. Name it in the PR body's security note for Jeff's sign-off (LINT-03).
